messages:
nisha: FYI customer report pasted below — nightly ingest pipeline started getting 429s around 02:05 UTC and some requests show high tail latency. They need a short-lived burst or guidance to avoid failing nightly jobs. Ticket #SUP-10298.

sam: Can you paste the raw headers or a sample request/response? need x-rate-limit headers + request-id to trace.

nisha: Paste from customer email: 

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-reproxxx
Content-Type: application/json

Response (partial):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 02:06:12 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1677901172
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c9f
Body: {"error":"Quota exceeded for free tier: concurrency or tokens"}
```

sam: OK thanks. Looks like they hit a token/concurrency cap. Customer says this happens only during nightly batch (approx 50k embeddings over 20m).

devon: Do we have their account id? can we check recent quota events and any automatic throttles?

nisha: Account id: acct_4452, email: infra-demo@custco.com. I checked console -> metrics: lots of 429 spikes at 02:00-02:30 UTC last 3 nights. No billing/upgrade on file.

sam: Repro suggestion for them: spread concurrent workers, add exponential backoff on 429, and use batch size 128 -> fewer requests. Also they can request a temporary demo burst.

julia-sales: @nisha I can fast-track a short demo uplift for them (7 days) but need expected TPS and token/day to size. What does the 50k embeddings translate to tokens?

nisha: Customer says ~50k embeddings, 1536-dim, that’s ~50k API calls if not batched. They can switch to batched embedding endpoint: each call can embed up to 2048 documents. They said existing pipeline is single-threaded line-by-line.

sam: Quick math: if they batch 256 docs per call => ~195 calls. If their concurrency is 20 workers that's ~10 qps sustained, should be fine. If not batching, 50k concurrent-ish bursts will blow the free-tier per-minute cap.

support-bot: Incident automation: Created support escalation ticket SE-789 for temporary burst approval workflow.

julia-sales: If they want a temporary bridge I can provision +sales-temporary-boost for 7 days. Need a small security review signoff from eng-security for any elevated quota. Devon can you confirm?

devon: Security is okay with a time-limited uplift for demo accounts as long as we log key actions and limit to non-production regions. I need request detail: start/end, inbound IP range (if they want locking), and the uplift caps (tokens/min, concurrency).

nisha: Customer provided target window: next 3 nights 02:00-03:00 UTC. Target peak: 2k requests/min; average 1k/min. They asked if we can enable a bump to 3k/min for that hour.

sam: Technically doable as a temporary exception. Two options: 1) Ask them to re-architect to batching + backoff (recommended); 2) Grant a one-off temporary burst (requires sales + security approval). If we grant, add a guard: autoswitched to fallback model (cheaper) if latency rises or error rate > 5%.

julia-sales: I'll propose 7-day demo uplift only for the 3x nightly window, with automatic expiry and monitoring. Need approval email thread. Nisha can you start the template with customer usage numbers?

nisha: Template ready, sending to @julia-sales now. Also adding recommended repro steps for engineering: 

1) Reproduce locally using the customer's pattern: 50k docs, 1 worker, no batching. Use curl script below to simulate throttling window.

```
# simulate 1000 parallel curl requests (example)
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"sample"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
wait
```
2) Capture response headers and ensure X-RateLimit-* logs are recorded.
3) If granting uplift, set temporary quota with soft-limit and alerting at 70% + automatic rollback at 110% of uplift.

sam: I'll add a small runbook snippet to the thread for on-call if we see cascading 429s: short-term mitigation = enable regional fallback + reduce concurrency via router policy.

devon: Thanks — I'll sign off on the security constraints. Julia, once you get the customer's acceptance we can fast-provision.

julia-sales: On it. I'll follow up with customer now and update the ticket. :thumbsup:
